first.rationale: Activation is down 6% QoQ and onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ—both signal friction in the user journey. Memory_31 showed signup simplification improved SMB activation durably, and memory_86 confirmed shortening onboarding lifted completion and time-to-value. Memory_91 indicates activation messaging also works, but onboarding friction appears to be the root lever here. Verifying memory_31 and memory_91 will confirm the magnitude of past gains and whether they're still reliable on the current product. A standard_experiment scaling a simplified onboarding path targets the immediate QoQ decline while preserving long-term retention quality—we avoid the promotional_pricing trap (which memory_73 warns requires careful cohort control) and focus on sustainable activation rather than margin erosion. Referral_incentive and enterprise_sales_assist are secondary levers; this week's constraint demands we address the core funnel friction first.
